reason: E2 shows that a protective oxide/spinel layer forms on a similar HEA at 800 °C, but it does not address the role of Cu content in forming this layer or its effect on dislocation activity and wear. E1 is about ML prediction and tension-compression asymmetry, providing no specific evidence for the oxide-dislocation-wear mechanism. The key premises linking Cu content to oxide stability, oxide to dislocation suppression, and dislocations to wear are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Reducing Cu content in FeNiCrCoCu HEA diminishes the formation of a continuous, adherent oxide/spinel layer at 800 °C.
A continuous oxide/spinel layer impedes dislocation nucleation and nano-plastic deformation during high-temperature sliding.
Increased dislocation activity leads to a directional increase in abrasive/adhesive wear rate.
